01 Build Ubuntu VM

  • Download the Ubuntu Server VM from the official repository

  • Create a new VM in VMWare

  • Choose the Ubuntu Server ISO file and proceed to next.

  • Once setup, install the Ubuntu Server from the Live ISO file.

  • SInce it’s a VM for a Lab environment, the server settings are pretty much straight forward.

  • Set up the username credentials and it starts installing.

  • Once the installation is completed. login to the Ubuntu Server

  • Next we will set up the Ubuntu server with the nexessary tools.

sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade -y

sudo apt install -y \
  curl \
  wget \
  vim \
  unzip \
  tar \
  jq \
  net-tools \
  python3 \
  python3-pip \
  python3-venv \
  chrony
  
sudo systemctl enable --now chrony
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname splunk-threat-lab
sudo mkdir -p /opt/threat-hunting-lab/{datasets,scripts,documentation,backups}

sudo mkdir -p /opt/threat-hunting-lab/datasets/{scenario_01,scenario_02,scenario_03}

sudo mkdir -p /opt/threat-hunting-lab/scripts/{generators,validation}

sudo chown -R $USER:$USER /opt/threat-hunting-lab
  • Once done, our directory structure should look the below;

02 Setting up SIEM

  • For the SIEM solution we will use splunk, hence we will set up the splunk enterprise free trial.

  • Install Splunk Enterprise

cd /tmp

wget -O splunk.deb \
"https://download.splunk.com/products/splunk/releases/10.6.1.1/linux/splunk-10.6.1.1-b2ae2962645c-linux-amd64.deb"

sudo dpkg -i splunk.deb

sudo useradd -r -M -d /opt/splunk -s /usr/sbin/nologin splunk

sudo chown -R splunk:splunk /opt/splunk

sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk start --accept-license

sudo /opt/splunk/bin/splunk enable boot-start \
-user splunk

Install it:

bash

sudo dpkg -i splunk.deb

The installation directory will be:

text

/opt/splunk

Configure the Splunk service account

We should avoid running Splunk as root.

Check whether the installation has created a dedicated user:

bash

id splunk

If the user does not exist, create it:

bash

sudo useradd -r -M -d /opt/splunk -s /usr/sbin/nologin splunk

Assign ownership:

bash

sudo chown -R splunk:splunk /opt/splunk

Start Splunk:

bash

sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk start --accept-license

During the initial startup, configure your Splunk administrator username and password.

Important: Use a unique administrator password. We will later create a separate participant account with limited permissions.

Enable Splunk to start automatically when Ubuntu boots:

bash

sudo /opt/splunk/bin/splunk enable boot-start \
-user splunk

Check the status:

bash

sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk status

The official installation procedure is documented here: Splunk Enterprise Linux Installation .

help.splunk.com

7. Step 5 – Access Splunk Web

bash

hostname -I

From your host computer, open:

text

http://VM-IP-ADDRESS:8000

You should see the Splunk login page.

Log in with the administrator credentials you created.

At this stage, we should have a functional standalone Splunk instance.

8. Step 6 – Validate the installation

Run these commands inside Ubuntu:

bash

# Check Splunk process
sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk status

# Check listening ports
sudo ss -lntp | grep -E '8000|8089'

# Check disk space
df -h

# Check memory
free -h

Step 1 — Install uv

Run this in your Linux terminal:

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

GitHub+1

source "$HOME/.local/bin/env"

uv --version

uv 0.x.x

The exact version may differ.

Step 2 — Clone EvidenceForge

First, choose where to keep the project. I recommend ~/tools.

mkdir -p ~/tools
cd ~/tools

Clone the official repository:

git clone https://github.com/Cisco-Talos/EvidenceForge.git

Enter the directory:

cd EvidenceForge

Verify:

pwd
git status

You should be inside:

/home/YOUR_USERNAME/tools/EvidenceForge

Install dependencies

Run:

uv sync

This creates an isolated Python virtual environment and installs EvidenceForge’s required dependencies.

It may take a few minutes.

Verify installation

Run:

uv run eforge version

Then:

uv run eforge --help

Expected result

You should see the EvidenceForge version and available CLI commands.

The official README confirms this installation sequence: git clone, cd EvidenceForge, uv sync.

GitHub+1

Official repository: Cisco Talos EvidenceForge

Step 3 - Install the AI authoring skills

First, make sure you’re in the repository:

cd ~/tools/EvidenceForge

Initialize the local configuration:

uv run eforge init

This creates a project-local config.yaml using the example configuration.

Verify the available commands:

uv run eforge --help

Install the AI authoring skills

EvidenceForge provides dedicated skills for scenario creation, validation, generation and evaluation.

Since you’re using GitHub Copilot, we’ll install the ChatGPT/Codex-compatible skills:

uv run eforge install-skills --agent chatgpt

This should create:

.agents/
└── skills/
    ├── eforge-scenario/
    ├── eforge-validate/
    ├── eforge-generate/
    ├── eforge-evaluate/
    └── ...

These are reusable instructions for AI agents. They aren’t a built-in Copilot extension, so we’ll use their contents as reference material in Copilot Chat.

Inspect the installation

Run:

uv run eforge version
uv run eforge info

Then:

ls -la .agents/skills/

Official documentation: EvidenceForge installation and agent skills.

Step 5 — Create your Null National Bank workspace

Keep your challenge definitions separate from the EvidenceForge installation:

mkdir -p ~/NullNationalBank/{scenarios,datasets,instructor,packs}

cd ~/NullNationalBank

Your structure:

NullNationalBank/

├── datasets/
├── instructor/
└── packs/

Verify and report back

Run:

ls -la ~/tools/EvidenceForge/.agents/skills/

ls -la ~/NullNationalBank/

Tell me:

  1. Did the skills install successfully?

  2. Are you using GitHub Copilot in VS Code?

Once confirmed, we’ll create the reusable Null National Bank organization pack with fictional employees, workstations, domain controllers, finance servers, network infrastructure and normal background activity. That environment will be reused across all your future detection challenges.

Hunters should connect the exfil destination to the part-1 DNS beaconing (update. / cdn.nullnationalbank.com subdomain encoding) — the domain was hostile from day one, but only proves hostile when tied to egress volume.
  • Fraud-prep reality check (stage 46): the skimmer is staging-only; payment-page production traffic was never touched. Debrief should emphasize that detection of intent vs. execution matters for regulatory reporting.
  • Phase 2 hunt (stages 48–50): the “clean” post-remediation log set should still show a disabled-not-deleted task on MN-FS01 and a single type-3 sqlsvc logon on MN-DB01. Teams that declare victory after remediation without spotting these two residuals have not finished the exercise.

What is WMIC ?

WMI is Windows Management Instrumentation is typically used for managing data in a windows operating system Its also highly efficient just like power shell since a user will be able to write scripts to automate tasks in a remote device. Due to this functionality its required to implement security features to prevent any unauthenticated services and operations.

Security with WMIC:

WMI security focuses on protecting access to namespace data. WMI first grants access to groups of users as specified by the WMI Control and DCOM settings and then providers determine if the user should have access to namespace data. Namespace security depends on standard Windows user security identifiers (SID) and the security descriptor for the WMI namespace. item.title: [04] DLL
item.description:
By: Prasanna | October 26, 2026

What is a DLL ?

DLL is known as Dynamic Link Library which provides most of the operating systems functionality. Lets, understand it in a simpler way. If you want to use a new font in notepad you should have the new font installed in your computer, similarly when any program runs in a windows computer it needs the supporting libraries to function properly which in this case is DLL files. You might have experienced errors such as DLL file missing, which we call it as a dependency issue, this happens when the required library file is not available for a process to run.

What is a RunDLL32 ?

Run Time DLL loads the required libraries during a runtime rather than importing all the DLL’s while a program is starting. Rundll32 is a 32 bit runtime DLL that can be loaded while a program is running, this is convenient for an attacker since they will be able to inject a malicious library function to obtain a reverse shell.

Reverse shell using Rundll32:

Given that we will be able to load malicious libraries into the victims device, an attacker will be able to obtain a reverse shell using various methods, we will explore a couple methods in this scenario,

  • Koadic Framework
  • Metasploit Framework
